findings.claim: All 42 practice questions across L1-L7 are typed “30+4 marks — Shakespeare Essay”.
findings.truth: DNA is a modern drama text on AQA 8702 Paper 2 Section A. The label must read “30+4 marks — Modern Text Essay”.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md, 'Specification at a glance': Paper 1 Section A is Shakespeare; Paper 2 Section A Modern texts, 'one essay question from a choice of two'. 3.2.1 lists Dennis Kelly.

findings.claim: Phil's plan is 'take a sample of Adam’s DNA from a jumper Adam was wearing, plant it on a fictional “postman” suspect'. Repeated in the Key Fact box, knowledge check 1 and flashcard 9.
findings.truth: The plan runs the other way. They burgle Adam's bedroom for his shoes and a jumper (without touching it), fake footprints in the woods with the shoes, and get a STRANGER'S DNA onto Adam's jumper by dropping it in the street for a passer-by to hand back. Brian gives the police the invented description.
findings.evidence: Act 1, wood. PHIL: 'find a pair of his shoes and an item of his clothing, a jumper ... do not touch the jumper' / 'you drop the jumper. The man picks it up, runs after you covering it in DNA'. Kelly, DNA (Faber/NT Connections script, full text): https://static1.squarespace.com/static/540b22a1e4b0d0f549866135/t/5a7b4ea8f9619af057028c51/1518030505202/DNA+-+FULL+PLAY.pdf

findings.claim: 'create a fake witness account using a man they found living rough in the woods' (L2 x2, knowledge check 4, flashcard 9); 'the man living rough has been arrested as a false witness' (L3).
findings.truth: No such man exists in the play. The false witness is Brian, a group member, who is made to say a fat postman with bad teeth exposed himself to him. The only person living rough is Adam himself, found in a hedge in Act 3. The man arrested is a real postman whose DNA Cathy took from the sorting office on her own initiative.
findings.evidence: Act 1: 'Brian, you cry ... you tell them a man showed you his willy in the woods'. Act 2, CATHY: 'A man down the sorting office ... we'll look for a fat balding postman with bad teeth.' Kelly, DNA (Faber/NT Connections script, full text): https://static1.squarespace.com/static/540b22a1e4b0d0f549866135/t/5a7b4ea8f9619af057028c51/1518030505202/DNA+-+FULL+PLAY.pdf

findings.claim: 'Someone threw him into a shaft, and he fell' (also the Key Fact box and flashcard 3).
findings.truth: Nobody throws Adam anywhere. They dare him to walk across a grille over a shaft, then pelt him with stones until he slips and drops through.
findings.evidence: Act 1, MARK: 'he's walked on the grille ... someone's pegged a stone at him ... really chucking these stones into him, really hard and laughing and he slips. And he drops.' findings.claim: 'John Tate bans the word “dead” and threatens: “I’m in charge. Everyone is happy. What am I?”' (the quotation also appears in the L2 question 5 mark scheme).
findings.truth: Misattributed and misquoted. 'I'm in charge. Everyone is happier. What's more important: one person or everyone?' is PHIL, in Act 3, justifying leaving Adam to die. John Tate's actual threat is to 'bite their face', and he pleads 'I am trying to keep everyone together.'
findings.evidence: 'I'm in charge' occurs once in the script, at Act 3 (Phil to Leah). Kelly, DNA (Faber/NT Connections script, full text): https://static1.squarespace.com/static/540b22a1e4b0d0f549866135/t/5a7b4ea8f9619af057028c51/1518030505202/DNA+-+FULL+PLAY.pdf

findings.claim: 'Danny and the others are on medication for anxiety and depression' (L3); 'Danny ... by Act 4, is on medication' (L4); 'Danny and Brian develop anxiety and depression' + Key Fact + flashcard 4 'He develops anxiety and needs medication by Act 4' (L6); L7 question 5 mark scheme 'Danny/medication'.
findings.truth: Danny is never medicated. Brian is. Danny's fate is work experience at a dentist's that he hates — the bitter end of his dental-college plan.
findings.evidence: Act 4, RICHARD: 'Danny's doing work experience as a dentist's. He hates it. ... Brian's on stronger and stronger medication. They caught him staring at a wall and drooling last week ... I think they're going to section him.' findings.claim: 'Richard asks: “What are you thinking?” Phil says nothing. The play ends on this image' (also flashcard 13: 'What question does Richard ask Phil at the very end of DNA?' → '“What are you thinking?”').
findings.truth: 'What are you thinking?' is LEAH's first line, Act 1, field. Richard's closing words are 'Come back, Phil. Phil?' before 'No answer. They sit in silence. End.'

findings.truth: Kelly's stage direction is the opposite, and the change is the point: 'PHIL is not eating. He stares into the distance.' He is also not alone — Richard is with him.

findings.truth: Cathy's television fame is Act 3, reported by Leah. By Act 4 she is running the group and has become violent.
findings.evidence: Act 3, LEAH: 'Cathy was on the telly. Used that clip on every channel. She's like a celebrity.' Act 4, RICHARD: 'Cathy doesn't care. She's too busy running things ... She's insane. findings.claim: 'the audience never hears his perspective' / 'Kelly's decision to keep Adam silent' + Key Fact + flashcard 14 (L4); 'Adam's silence — he barely appears and never speaks in a meaningful way' + 'Adam's silence is imposed' + flashcard 11 (L6).
findings.truth: Adam speaks at length in the Act 3 wood scene. He gives a long, broken account of falling, waking in the dark, drinking his own blood, and building a hedge home, and refuses to come back. His near-absence is real; his silence is not.
findings.evidence: Act 3, ADAM: 'I was in a Dark ... I woke up with liquor on my head ... I found my place where I live ... I'm not coming back.' findings.truth: By Act 3 he has only stopped appearing ('John Tate hasn't been seen in weeks'). The conversion is reported in Act 4: he has 'found God' and joined the Jesus Army.

findings.truth: The street scene is scene one OF each act, inside it, not a prologue placed before it. Acts 1-3 run street / field / wood / field; Act 4 runs street / field.

findings.claim: 'Richard, who at the end tries to resist, mirrors those who eventually refused the experimenter's orders.'
findings.truth: Richard never refuses Phil. His only pushback is to John Tate in Act 1 ('You shouldn't threaten me, John') and a nervous 'Er, Phil' in Act 2. At the end he is begging Phil to come back and run the group again.

findings.claim: 'The exact nature of Phil's instructions is left ambiguous by Kelly. The audience must infer what happens from the characters' reactions and the events of Act 4.'
findings.truth: The order is staged, not inferred. Phil pulls a plastic bag over Brian's head to demonstrate the method, tells Brian to do whatever Cathy says, and sends the pair off to 'make a game of it' with Adam. Only the killing itself is offstage.

findings.claim: Three glossary terms carry another term's definition: 'conscience' is defined as the moral of a story (L2); 'textual evidence' is defined as a thesis (L7); 'bonobos' is defined as 'a brief, memorable phrase used as evidence in an essay' (L7).
findings.truth: Each definition has been rewritten to match its own term. The definitions appear both in the hover data-def and in glossary_terms.
findings.evidence: Internal consistency; the bonobo definition contradicts L2, L5 and L7, which all correctly gloss bonobos as apes.

findings.claim: Model exam reference: 'when Phil calmly outlines his plan while eating an ice cream' (L2 exam tip, L7 as a worked paraphrase example).
findings.truth: Wrong scene. The ice cream belongs to the Act 1 field scene with Leah. In the wood Phil sets his Coke down, delivers the plan, then bends down, picks it up and drinks it — which makes the same point better.
findings.evidence: Act 1, wood: 'PHIL puts his Coke carefully on the ground' ... 'He bends down. Picks up his Coke.' Kelly, DNA (Faber/NT Connections script, full text): https://static1.squarespace.com/static/540b22a1e4b0d0f549866135/t/5a7b4ea8f9619af057028c51/1518030505202/DNA+-+FULL+PLAY.pdf

findings.claim: All 42 mark schemes tie the SPaG mark to the content band: 'Top band (26-30 marks + 4 spelling/grammar)', 'Mid band (11-15 marks + 2 spelling/grammar)', and so on.
findings.truth: AQA awards the 4 SPaG marks independently of the content level (threshold 1, intermediate 2-3, high performance 4). A weak essay in accurate English can still take 4. Two defensible corrections: (a) strip the SPaG figures from the band ladders and add one line stating the SPaG bands; or (b) restate each band as 'plus up to 4 for SPaG, judged separately'. Option (a) is cleaner but rewrites 42 long strings; option (b) is lighter. Recommend (a), run as its own sweep because the same ladder template is used across other English Literature units.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md, AO4 is a separate objective; AQA mark schemes score SPaG on a separate scale.

findings.claim: 'dramatic uncertainty' appears twice in L2 glossary_terms (index 0 and index 4), with identical definitions.
findings.truth: A duplicate row. Harmless to a student, worth tidying if the loader ever dedupes.

findings.claim: 'In Act 3, she [Cathy] reports back from the woods with visible excitement, describing events in graphic terms.'
findings.truth: Cathy's Act 3 report is matter-of-fact — she describes Adam's hedge complex. The manic excitement in that scene is Brian's. Not wrong enough to edit, but the sentence overstates the text.
findings.evidence: Act 3, wood. Kelly, DNA (Faber/NT Connections script, full text): https://static1.squarespace.com/static/540b22a1e4b0d0f549866135/t/5a7b4ea8f9619af057028c51/1518030505202/DNA+-+FULL+PLAY.pdf

summary: The exam claims survive checking: Paper 2 Section A, one essay from a choice of two, 30 marks + 4 SPaG, AO1 12 / AO2 12 / AO3 6, no extract, closed book, ~45 minutes — all correct in L1 and L7, so the 30 Aug AO2-denial fix has held. The play content has not survived it: the cover-up plan is described backwards, an invented 'man living rough' is used as the false witness in three lessons, Adam is said to be thrown down the shaft, Phil's Act 3 line 'I'm in charge' is given to John Tate, Richard's closing line is actually Leah's opening one, Danny is medicated instead of Brian, Cathy goes into television instead of taking over, and Adam is said never to speak when he has the play's longest speech. 23 findings (10 HIGH, 11 MEDIUM, 2 LOW), 107 edits, no lesson clean. One ADJUDICATE: the 42 mark-scheme band ladders tie the SPaG mark to the content band, which AQA does not.
